title: MLflow requirement inference for sklearn-based and skops models: cloudpickle is logged transitively via joblib>=1.6.0, so do not assert it is absent
answers: Why is the lightgbm skops cross-version test failing on a cloudpickle assertion after joblib 1.6.0?
Which requirements end up in requirements.txt for a skops-serialized sklearn or lightgbm model?
Where is the cloudpickle-absence check in the skops save/load tests for lightgbm models?
body:
Path: Tests that save and reload sklearn-wrapper and lightgbm sklearn models serialized with skops, and check the inferred requirements.txt that mlflow.lightgbm logs for them; chokepoint tests/lightgbm/test_lightgbm_model_export.py:test_sklearn_model_save_load_by_skops (and test_sklearn_regressor_model_save_load_by_skops).
Rule: joblib>=1.6.0 replaced its vendored joblib.externals.cloudpickle with a runtime dependency on the standalone cloudpickle package and imports it at import time. Because scikit-learn depends on joblib, requirement inference records cloudpickle==<version> for any sklearn-based model regardless of serialization format. Do not assert cloudpickle is absent from logged requirements in these tests; keep the positive skops==<version> check and the reload/predict assertions.
Symptom: The daily cross-version-tests job for lightgbm models turned red (from 2026-09-02) after joblib 1.6.0 was released, failing on the `cloudpickle not in logged_reqs` assertion.
Constraints: Applies to environments with joblib>=1.6.0. Under joblib 1.5.x cloudpickle is not imported transitively, so the absence held there; the tests should not depend on the joblib version either way. Not a general statement about every mlflow flavor's requirements.
applies: Test-only guidance for assertions on logged requirements.txt contents of sklearn-based models in the lightgbm/sklearn skops tests.
says: Saved models unexpectedly list extra serialization libraries in their recorded environment dependencies.
Model verification tests fail when checking that certain packaging tools are omitted from requirements.
search: In tests/lightgbm/test_lightgbm_model_export.py skops tests, assertions must not expect cloudpickle to be absent from logged requirements because joblib>=1.6.0 imports cloudpickle as a standalone runtime dependency. Because scikit-learn depends on joblib, requirement inference transitively records cloudpickle for all sklearn-based models regardless of serialization format. This test-only rule applies to environments with joblib>=1.6.0 and maintains positive skops version and reload assertions without altering general flavor requirement inference.
